tasks.title: GSD of a nadir camera
tasks.statement: The camera looks straight down from a height of **{h} m**. The effective pixel of the mode is **{p} µm**, the focal length is **{f} mm**. Find the GSD in centimeters per pixel.
tasks.solution: GSD = h·p/f; in consistent units: h [m]·p [µm]/f [mm] = mm/px, divide by 10 for cm/px. The module example: a CM3 in 2304×1296 (2.8 µm, 4.74 mm) at 50 m gives 2.95 cm/px.

tasks.title: Pixels on target
tasks.statement: Camera: effective pixel **{p} µm**, f = **{f} mm**, nadir, height **{h} m**. How many pixels does an object **{d} m** wide span?
tasks.solution: N = d/GSD = d·f/(h·p). The module example: 0.5 m at 50 m with a CM3 in 2304×1296 is 17 px, below the 20–30 px guideline for a detector; with a CM3 Wide (2.75 mm), 10 px.

tasks.title: Blur from rotation
tasks.statement: Focal length in pixels **f_px = {fpx}**, exposure **1/{inv} s**, the vehicle rotates at **{w}°/s** across the optical axis. Find the blur in pixels.
tasks.solution: Blur = ω·t·f_px, with ω in rad/s. The module example: 90°/s, 1/500 s, f_px 1693 → 1.571·0.002·1693 = 5.32 px, eight times the translational blur from 10 m/s at 50 m.
